newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein leader's UK parliament visit condemned.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein leader's UK parliament visit condemned.

text.p: A planned private visit to Britain's parliament by Irish republican leader Gerry Adams drew strong criticism on Wednesday and the opposition Labour party condemned one of its own legislators for inviting him.

The leader of Sinn Fein, political wing of the Irish Republican Army (IRA), had hoped to launch his autobiography on Thursday in the building where the House of Commons (lower house of parliament) is located. But the launch was cancelled by parliamentary officials last weekend.
Left-wing Labour member of parliament Jeremy Corbyn, however, announced he would host a private meeting with Adams on Thursday instead.
Labour officials said on Wednesday they might throw Corbyn out of the party if the meeting took place in the parliament building.
"We utterly condemn his proposed action. If he persists it will be a matter for disciplinary action," Donald Dewar, Labour's chief parliamentary business manager, said.
"It is particularly reprehensible in the light of recent events involving the IRA," Dewar said.
On Monday, British police foiled what they said was an imminent IRA bomb attack, arresting five people and shooting dead one man in dawn raids in London.
The IRA has fought to oust Britain from Northern Ireland.

Adams was elected member of the British parliament for West Belfast in the 1980s but never took his seat in the House of Commons. He said he regarded Britain as an occupying power in the province and he has refused to take an oath of allegiance to the British monarch.
But he has visited parliament several times in recent years and cannot be barred because he is a former MP.
